links.outcome: Semantic similarity to reference answers across RAG configurations, including database size and embedding model
links.effect: Larger database sizes significantly improved semantic similarity (size 5: +0.043, p = 0.001); bge-large-en-v1.5 improved performance (p = 0.0016); Bio_ClinicalBERT reduced it (p < 0.001). Mean similarity up to 0.786.
links.quote: Larger database sizes significantly improved semantic similarity, with the largest gain at intermediate sizes (e.g., size 5: +0.043, p = 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Selecting lightweight open-source models and RAG configurations (embedding model, chunk size, database size) for low-resource settings

screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks different lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) configurations (embedding models, database size, chunk size) to evaluate grounding and hallucination reduction for clinical Q&A in resource-constrained environments.
